generation.final_prompt:
Rendering style:
Create an authored editorial illustration for a serious technology newspaper.

Direction:
- authored editorial print language
- deliberate simplified shapes with clear focal hierarchy
- restrained limited palette
- subtle physical print texture
- controlled abstraction and strong negative space
- non-photorealistic but factually grounded representation
- newspaper and social-card readability

Fixed factual and safety restrictions:
- Do not render visible text, captions, headlines, or newspaper typography.
- Do not render logos or trademarks.
- Do not fabricate visible factual evidence.
- Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
- Do not imitate a named or living artist.

Profile-specific exclusions:
- glossy CGI
- luxury product render
- generic futuristic concept art
- cyberpunk or neon
- glowing circuit-board decoration
- floating particles
- heroic centered hardware
- server rack treated as monument or skyscraper
- generic server room
- advertising composition
- airbrushed gradients
- synthetic chrome
- excessive pseudo-technical detail
- malformed or visible text
- labels
- diagrams with words

Exact source facts:
Title: OPENAI REWRITES SAFETY FRAMEWORK AS LARGEST TRAINING RUN STAYS PAUSED
Summary: OpenAI is rewriting its Preparedness Framework while expanding monitoring, strengthening research-environment isolation, and moving alignment work earlier in model training. It has resumed many smaller or lower-risk workloads after a pause of little more than two weeks, but the largest planned frontier reinforcement-learning run and significant Astra and cyber workloads remain paused. Astra is an unreleased model that may reach OpenAI's Critical cyber threshold. OpenAI has not released the promised technical postmortem of the Hugging Face breach or the evidence behind Astra's possible Critical classification.

Editorial idea:
Frontier AI development is being slowed and reshaped as safety monitoring catches up with expanding capabilities.

Central subject:
OpenAI's paused frontier training and revised safety controls

Visual relationship:
A powerful process continues in smaller lanes while its largest route remains blocked for safety review.

Composition:
Show a large industrial process line narrowing into several monitored channels, with the biggest channel visibly halted behind a barrier and smaller channels continuing under observation. Keep the scene grounded in physical infrastructure rather than depicting abstract AI imagery.

Permitted literal elements:
A stopped main conveyor or process lane
Smaller active lanes branching around it
Inspection stations with human observers
A clear safety barrier around the halted lane

Abstraction level:
medium

Story-specific forbidden elements:
Racks
Chips
Laptops
Robots
Clouds
Shields
Arrows
Charts
Skyscrapers
Chess
Handshakes
Split-screen conflict
Rendered text
Logos
Unsupported physical details

Likely failure modes to avoid:
Depicting AI as a humanoid machine
Making the image a generic data-center scene
Showing all training stopped when the report says smaller workloads resumed
Using warning symbols without showing the specific tension between resumed work and the paused large

Global factual restrictions:
Do not fabricate visible factual evidence. Do not imitate a named or living artist. Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
Do not render any words, letters, numbers, labels, captions, annotations, signage, diagrams with text, logos, watermarks, or pseudo-writing anywhere in the image.
If the concept cannot be represented without visible text, represent the relationship through shape, scale, spacing, direction, grouping, interruption, containment, or contrast instead.
